chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, from Abu Khadija, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the house in which there is a wedding, and hates the house in which there is a divorce. And there is nothing more hateful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, than divorce.

key_terms.الطَّلَاقُ: Divorce (al-talaq) — the legal dissolution of marriage
key_terms.الْعُرْسُ: Wedding/marriage celebration (al-urs) — the joyous union of spouses
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: A divine epithet meaning 'Mighty and Majestic', commonly used in hadith when referring to God

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about divorce according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys that God loves the household in which marriage is celebrated but despises the household in which divorce occurs, making divorce the most detested act in God's sight. This hadith reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that divorce, while legally permitted, is strongly discouraged (makruh) especially when the spouses are compatible. The Imam's audience would have understood this as a strong moral deterrent against hasty or unnecessary divorce, reinforcing the sanctity of the marital bond.
